metadata.title: HPC Job Lifecycle Security

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for governing the security of high-performance computing jobs throughout submission, scheduling, execution, and completion.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: HPC batch schedulers, job submission pipelines, execution environments, pre- and post-job hooks, and job state management systems.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Pattern for securing the lifecycle of scheduler-mediated HPC jobs, treating jobs as first-class security objects.

props.name: depends-on
props.remarks: Job lifecycle security assumes trusted scheduler-mediated execution on shared HPC platforms.

props.name: depends-on
props.remarks: Job lifecycle security relies on correct attribution and authorization of job submitters and scheduler identities.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: HPC job lifecycle, scheduler abuse, and insider threat considerations as defined by NIST SP 800-234.

metadata.remarks: HPC Job Lifecycle Security defines trust properties required to ensure that job submission, scheduling, execution, and teardown in high-performance computing environments do not become abuse paths. This pattern models jobs themselves as security-relevant objects, recognizing that legitimate jobs can be malicious without exploiting software vulnerabilities.

components.title: HPC Job Submission Validation
components.description: Validation and constraint of job submission artifacts, parameters, and execution context.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Execution of unauthorized or malicious commands via job submission scripts or parameters.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Validation and restriction of job scripts, parameters, and submission metadata.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Restricted and reviewed modification of job submission mechanisms.
Input validation for job submission interfaces.

components.title: HPC Job Execution Context Control
components.description: Restriction and governance of environment variables, execution context, and runtime privileges associated with HPC jobs.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Hijacking of execution flow via manipulated environment variables or runtime context.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Controlled and sanitized execution environments for scheduled HPC jobs.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Least privilege enforced for job execution contexts.
Least functionality enforced within job execution environments.

components.title: HPC Job State and Transition Governance
components.description: Governance of job state transitions, chaining, dependencies, and completion semantics.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Abuse of scheduler state transitions or job dependencies to gain unauthorized execution.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Controlled and auditable state transitions for scheduler-managed jobs.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Enforcement of authorized behavior through scheduler-managed state transitions.
Audit logging of job execution states and transitions.
